summary: Estimate nₖ with a better upper bound than Cambie's nₖ ≤ k · lcm(1, …, k − 1).
problem: Estimate nₖ by finding a better upper bound than Cambie's nₖ ≤ k · lcm(1, …, k − 1).

notes.title: Formalization note
notes.text: The comparator takes its least common multiple in ℕ and casts the result. Writing the ascription as `((…).lcm (fun n : ℕ => n) : ℝ)` instead puts it on the `Finset.lcm` application, so the coercion lands on n and the lcm is taken in ℝ. There the lcm of non-zero elements is 1, and the whole comparator collapses to k.

title: Erdős Problem #1063
